title: Capacity-aware traffic tiling and compatibility probes for fault-tolerant model rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our existing rollout primitives (simple percent-based canaries + basic fallback to older model) do not handle multi-dimensional constraints like region capacity tiers, model variant incompatibility for KV cache formats, and session affinity. This ticket proposes a new rollout orchestration pattern: capacity-aware traffic tiling + compatibility probes. Goals: 1) avoid unsafe variant activation that causes silent semantic regressions or cache-miss spikes, 2) make rollouts resilient to regional capacity exhaustion by degrading gracefully, and 3) enable deterministic session-affine A/B experiments without overloading a single capacity tier. The feature is intended to sit in the deployment controller and routing layer and coordinate with autoscaling, the runtime compatibility matrix, and the console rollout UI.
acceptance_criteria: New rollout controller accepts 'tiling' policy for traffic distribution with parameters: tile_size, affinity_key, cap_tiers.
Compatibility probe framework can run synthetic probes (KV warmup, prefix tasks, max-seq tests) against a model variant and publish a pass/fail + metrics bucket within 60s.
Automated rollback triggers defined and enforced: latency p50 > baseline * 1.20 for 5m OR error rate increase >0.5% absolute OR semantic score drop on golden set >2 points.

When primary region capacity tier is full, controller shifts tiles to fallback tiers in this order: compatible quantized variant (same region) -> warm cross-region pool -> degraded short-output mode -> rate-limited queue. No requests are routed to incompatible variants.
Dashboard shows per-tile metrics (latency, errors, semantic score, cost) and alerting on rollback thresholds.
progress_updates: 2026-01-14: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype 'tile' abstraction that maps hash ranges -> capacity_tier buckets. Verified basic affinity preservation across 10k synthetic sessions.

2026-01-21: Compatibility probe spec finalized after runtime review. Probe types: cold-start KV-warmup, prefix continuity, generation-quality on golden set. Probe runs return delta_metrics and compatibility_score.
2026-01-26: Integration tests added: canary with tile_size=1% + affinity_key=user_id reproduced session-affine behavior and maintained latency SLO in unit clusters.

2026-01-29: Danger case discovered in staging: cross-region fallback to a quantized variant caused subtle tokenization differences for a multi-lingual model. Decision: add tokenizer-normalization probe before allowing cross-variant routing; block routing if tokenizer mismatch >0.1% on probe samples.
2026-02-02: Auto-rollback thresholds tuned (p50 20% / error +0.5% / semantic -2pts). Preparing canary with internal-only shadowing for 24h prior to public canary.
2026-02-03: PRs opened for rollout-controller and probe harness. Requesting runtime and platform review; preparing demo for PM review next week.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use tiling (small fixed hash ranges) rather than purely percent-based sampling to preserve session affinity and avoid noisy traffic spikes when autoscaling rebalances nodes.
Trade-off: Tile preservation increases complexity for extremely fine-grained experiments. We cap minimum tile_size at 0.5% to avoid thousands of micro-tiles in a single rollout.
Compatibility scoring: lightweight fast probes run first (tokenizer match, kv-warmup latency) then generation-quality probes run asynchronously and can pause ramp if semantic delta > threshold.
Fallback ordering chosen to minimize user-visible regressions: prefer same-region compatible variants (quantized) over cross-region to reduce latency penalties.
Manual override: Operators can force an immediate region-evacuation policy for incidents, bypassing tiling rebalancer. This will trigger an incident playbook.
test_plan: Unit tests for tile hashing and affinity mapping.
Staging canary: internal shadow for 24h, then 1% tile canary for 2h with synthetic probes enabled.
A/B experiment: run 5% tile vs baseline for 48h with cost and semantic metrics recorded.
Failure injection: simulate regional capacity drain and assert correct fallback ordering and no routing to incompatible variants.
